title: Core beliefs
description: Global, rigid beliefs about the self (helpless, unlovable and worthless clusters, plus adaptive counterparts), others, the world and the future. Fills the core belief slot of the cognitive conceptualization diagram and longitudinal formulations. Each concept carries about: self, others, world or future.
sources: Beck-2021 § Ch. 17 Introduction to Beliefs
Beck-2021 § Ch. 18 Modifying Beliefs
BeckInstitute-Worksheet-Packet-2020 § Core Beliefs About the Self
Beck-etal-2024 § Ch. 7 Schemas: Core Beliefs and Underlying Assumptions
Young-etal-2003 § Ch. 1 Schema Therapy: Conceptual Model (early maladaptive schemas)
Beck-etal-2015 § Ch. 2 Theory of Personality Disorders

concepts.label: Helpless
concepts.definition: Umbrella self-belief of being ineffective: unable to get things done, protect oneself, or measure up to others.
concepts.client_wording: Deep down I feel I can't cope or handle things.
concepts.example: "I can't cope with any of this."
sources: Beck-2021 § Ch. 17 Introduction to Beliefs
BeckInstitute-Worksheet-Packet-2020 § Core Beliefs About the Self

concepts.label: Incompetent
concepts.definition: Belief that one lacks the basic ability to get things done or handle responsibilities, regardless of effort.
concepts.client_wording: I'm useless; I can't do things properly.
concepts.example: "I'll mess this up like I mess everything up."
sources: BeckInstitute-Worksheet-Packet-2020 § Core Beliefs About the Self
BeckInstitute-Worksheet-Packet-2020 § Cognitive Conceptualization Diagram Example and Case Write-Up

concepts.label: Needy and dependent
alt_labels: I can't manage on my own
concepts.definition: Belief that one is weak and cannot function, decide or manage daily life without substantial help from others.
concepts.client_wording: I can't manage on my own; I need someone to look after me.
concepts.example: "I couldn't survive if my partner left."
sources: BeckInstitute-Worksheet-Packet-2020 § Core Beliefs About the Self
Beck-etal-2015 § Ch. 8 Dependent Personality Disorder
Young-etal-2003 § Ch. 1 Schema Therapy: Conceptual Model (early maladaptive schemas)

concepts.label: Vulnerable
concepts.definition: Belief that one is weak and unable to protect oneself, so harm, illness or catastrophe is likely.
concepts.client_wording: I can't protect myself; something bad is bound to happen to me.
concepts.example: "If something goes wrong, I won't be able to handle it and I'll get hurt."
sources: BeckInstitute-Worksheet-Packet-2020 § Core Beliefs About the Self
Young-etal-2003 § Ch. 1 Schema Therapy: Conceptual Model (early maladaptive schemas)

concepts.label: Powerless or trapped
concepts.definition: Belief that one has no control over one's life or oneself, and is stuck or trapped with no way out.
concepts.client_wording: I have no control; I'm trapped and nothing I do changes anything.
concepts.example: "I'm stuck in this situation and there's nothing I can do."
sources: BeckInstitute-Worksheet-Packet-2020 § Core Beliefs About the Self
Beck-2021 § Ch. 17 Introduction to Beliefs

concepts.label: A failure
concepts.definition: Global judgment that one has failed in life or in important roles, drawn from falling short in achievement.
concepts.client_wording: I'm a failure; I've messed up my life.
concepts.example: "I'm unemployed and divorced. I'm a total failure."
sources: BeckInstitute-Worksheet-Packet-2020 § Core Beliefs About the Self
BeckInstitute-Worksheet-Packet-2020 § Cognitive Conceptualization Diagram Example and Case Write-Up
Young-etal-2003 § Ch. 1 Schema Therapy: Conceptual Model (early maladaptive schemas)

concepts.label: Inferior to others
concepts.definition: Belief that one is less capable or less adequate than other people, reached by comparing oneself with them.
concepts.client_wording: Everyone else is better than me.
concepts.example: "Everyone at work is smarter and more capable than me."
sources: BeckInstitute-Worksheet-Packet-2020 § Core Beliefs About the Self

concepts.label: Not good enough
concepts.definition: Belief that one never meets the required standard in achievement or performance, however much one does.
concepts.client_wording: Whatever I do, it's never good enough.
concepts.example: "I got a B. I'm just not good enough."
sources: BeckInstitute-Worksheet-Packet-2020 § Core Beliefs About the Self
Beck-2021 § Ch. 17 Introduction to Beliefs

concepts.label: Unlovable
concepts.definition: Umbrella self-belief that one lacks the qualities that would make others love, want or care about one.
concepts.client_wording: Deep down I feel nobody could really love me.
concepts.example: "No one could ever love someone like me."
sources: Beck-2021 § Ch. 17 Introduction to Beliefs
BeckInstitute-Worksheet-Packet-2020 § Core Beliefs About the Self

concepts.label: Unlikeable or boring
concepts.definition: Belief that one is socially dull or disagreeable, with nothing to offer, so others will not like or choose one.
concepts.client_wording: People find me boring; I've got nothing to offer.
concepts.example: "Nobody wants to talk to me at parties."
sources: BeckInstitute-Worksheet-Packet-2020 § Core Beliefs About the Self
Leigh-Clark-2018 § The Clark and Wells (1995) model

concepts.label: Unwanted or unimportant
concepts.definition: Belief that one does not matter to others and is not wanted, valued or cared for.
concepts.client_wording: I don't matter to anyone.
concepts.example: "If I disappeared, no one would even notice."
sources: BeckInstitute-Worksheet-Packet-2020 § Core Beliefs About the Self

concepts.label: Unattractive or undesirable
concepts.definition: Belief that one is physically or sexually undesirable, so others will find one unappealing.
concepts.client_wording: I'm ugly; no one would find me attractive.
concepts.example: "No one would ever want to date me looking like this."
sources: BeckInstitute-Worksheet-Packet-2020 § Core Beliefs About the Self

concepts.label: Different, does not belong
concepts.definition: Belief that one is fundamentally different from other people and does not fit in or belong to any group.
concepts.client_wording: I'm different from everyone; I don't fit in anywhere.
concepts.example: "I'm weird. I've never belonged anywhere."
sources: BeckInstitute-Worksheet-Packet-2020 § Core Beliefs About the Self
Young-etal-2003 § Ch. 1 Schema Therapy: Conceptual Model (early maladaptive schemas)
Leigh-Clark-2018 § The Clark and Wells (1995) model

concepts.label: Defective or flawed
concepts.definition: Belief that something is basically wrong with one, a hidden flaw that would cause rejection if others saw it.
concepts.client_wording: There's something wrong with me, and if people saw it they'd reject me.
concepts.example: "There's something wrong with me that other people don't have."
sources: BeckInstitute-Worksheet-Packet-2020 § Core Beliefs About the Self
Young-etal-2003 § Ch. 1 Schema Therapy: Conceptual Model (early maladaptive schemas)

concepts.label: Bound to be rejected or abandoned
concepts.definition: Belief that, because of who one is, others will inevitably reject or abandon one, leaving one alone.
concepts.client_wording: Sooner or later everyone will leave me, and I'll end up alone.
concepts.example: "He'll get bored of me and leave, like everyone does."
sources: BeckInstitute-Worksheet-Packet-2020 § Core Beliefs About the Self
Young-etal-2003 § Ch. 1 Schema Therapy: Conceptual Model (early maladaptive schemas)

concepts.label: Worthless
concepts.definition: Umbrella self-belief that one has no value as a person, or is morally bad, unacceptable or undeserving.
concepts.client_wording: Deep down I feel I'm worthless as a person.
concepts.example: "I'm worthless. I'm a waste of space."
sources: Beck-2021 § Ch. 17 Introduction to Beliefs
BeckInstitute-Worksheet-Packet-2020 § Core Beliefs About the Self

concepts.label: Bad or immoral
concepts.definition: Belief that one is morally bad, wicked or sinful at the core, not just someone who has done wrong things.
concepts.client_wording: I'm a bad person deep down.
concepts.example: "Good people don't do what I did. I'm rotten inside."
sources: BeckInstitute-Worksheet-Packet-2020 § Core Beliefs About the Self

concepts.label: Dangerous or toxic
concepts.definition: Belief that one is harmful, toxic or evil and a threat to others; often found behind harm-related obsessions.
concepts.client_wording: There's something evil or toxic in me that could hurt people.
concepts.example: "Maybe I'm the kind of person who could hurt a child."
sources: BeckInstitute-Worksheet-Packet-2020 § Core Beliefs About the Self
Rachman-1997 § Misinterpretation of the significance of intrusive thoughts

concepts.label: Crazy or abnormal
concepts.definition: Belief that one is mentally unbalanced, abnormal or going mad, often taken as confirmed by one's symptoms.
concepts.client_wording: I'm crazy; my mind isn't normal.
concepts.example: "Normal people don't have thoughts like mine. I must be crazy."
sources: BeckInstitute-Worksheet-Packet-2020 § Core Beliefs About the Self

concepts.label: Undeserving
concepts.definition: Belief that one does not deserve care, happiness or good things, at the extreme not deserving to live; prompts risk assessment.
concepts.client_wording: I don't deserve anything good.
concepts.example: "Why would I treat myself? I don't deserve it."
sources: BeckInstitute-Worksheet-Packet-2020 § Core Beliefs About the Self

concepts.label: Reasonably competent
concepts.definition: Adaptive self-belief that one is reasonably competent, in control and able to cope, with ordinary strengths and weaknesses.
concepts.client_wording: I can handle most things reasonably well.
concepts.example: "I'm not perfect, but I can usually cope."
sources: BeckInstitute-Worksheet-Packet-2020 § Core Beliefs About the Self
Beck-2021 § Ch. 18 Modifying Beliefs
Padesky-1994 § Constructing new schemas

concepts.label: Reasonably lovable
concepts.definition: Adaptive self-belief that one is reasonably likeable, wanted and good enough to be loved, and unlikely to end up alone.
concepts.client_wording: People can like and love me as I am.
concepts.example: "My friends enjoy my company, even when I'm quiet."
sources: BeckInstitute-Worksheet-Packet-2020 § Core Beliefs About the Self
Beck-2021 § Ch. 18 Modifying Beliefs
Padesky-1994 § Constructing new schemas

concepts.label: Worthwhile
concepts.definition: Adaptive self-belief that one is reasonably worthwhile, acceptable and good as a person, despite mistakes.
concepts.client_wording: I'm an okay person who has value, even when I get things wrong.
concepts.example: "I made a mistake, but I'm still a decent person."
sources: BeckInstitute-Worksheet-Packet-2020 § Core Beliefs About the Self
Beck-2021 § Ch. 18 Modifying Beliefs
Padesky-1994 § Constructing new schemas

concepts.label: Others are untrustworthy or dangerous
concepts.definition: Belief that other people will hurt, deceive, humiliate or exploit one if given the chance.
concepts.client_wording: People can't be trusted; they'll hurt or use me if I let them.
concepts.example: "If I let my guard down, people will take advantage."
sources: Young-etal-2003 § Ch. 1 Schema Therapy: Conceptual Model (early maladaptive schemas)
Foa-etal-1999 § Negative Cognitions About the World factor
Beck-etal-2015 § Ch. 12 Paranoid, Schizotypal, and Schizoid Personality Disorders

concepts.label: Others are critical and judgmental
concepts.definition: Belief that other people are quick to criticize, judge or reject, and are watching for one's faults.
concepts.client_wording: People are judgmental and always looking for my faults.
concepts.example: "Everyone in the meeting will notice I'm nervous and judge me."
sources: Beck-etal-2015 § Ch. 9 Avoidant Personality Disorder
Leigh-Clark-2018 § The Clark and Wells (1995) model
BeckInstitute-Worksheet-Packet-2020 § Cognitive Conceptualization Diagram Example and Case Write-Up

concepts.label: Others are uncaring
alt_labels: no one will be there for me
concepts.definition: Belief that other people will not give care, understanding or support when one needs it.
concepts.client_wording: Nobody really cares; I can't expect support from anyone.
concepts.example: "There's no point telling anyone. They won't care."
sources: Young-etal-2003 § Ch. 1 Schema Therapy: Conceptual Model (early maladaptive schemas)

concepts.label: Others are unreliable
concepts.definition: Belief that other people are inconsistent and will let one down or leave, so relationships cannot be counted on.
concepts.client_wording: People always let you down or leave in the end.
concepts.example: "Everyone leaves eventually, so why get close?"
sources: Young-etal-2003 § Ch. 1 Schema Therapy: Conceptual Model (early maladaptive schemas)

concepts.label: Others are controlling or intrusive
concepts.definition: Belief that other people will dominate, control or intrude on one, so independence must be guarded.
concepts.client_wording: If I let people close, they'll try to control me.
concepts.example: "If I tell my boss my plans, she'll take over."
sources: Beck-etal-2015 § Ch. 12 Paranoid, Schizotypal, and Schizoid Personality Disorders
Beck-etal-2015 § Ch. 13 Passive-Aggressive Personality Disorder (Negativistic Personality Disorder)

concepts.label: Others are incompetent or irresponsible
concepts.definition: Belief that other people are careless, irresponsible or incompetent, so one must check or do things oneself.
concepts.client_wording: Other people are careless; if I want it done right, I do it myself.
concepts.example: "I can't delegate this. They'll only get it wrong."
sources: Beck-etal-2015 § Ch. 10 Obsessive-Compulsive Personality Disorder

concepts.label: Others are inferior
alt_labels: people are there to be used
concepts.definition: Belief that other people are weaker, lesser or there to be used, linked to entitlement in some personality presentations.
concepts.client_wording: Most people just aren't on my level.
concepts.example: "Rules are for ordinary people, not for me."
sources: Beck-etal-2015 § Ch. 14 Narcissistic Personality Disorder
Beck-etal-2015 § Ch. 16 Antisocial Personality Disorder
Young-etal-2003 § Ch. 1 Schema Therapy: Conceptual Model (early maladaptive schemas)

concepts.label: The world is dangerous
concepts.definition: Belief that the world is full of threat, so harm can strike at any time and constant vigilance is needed.
concepts.client_wording: The world is a dangerous place; nowhere is really safe.
concepts.example: "Since the attack, I know anything can happen to anyone, anywhere."
sources: Ehlers-Clark-2000 § Excessively negative appraisals and sense of current threat
Foa-etal-1999 § Negative Cognitions About the World factor

concepts.label: The world is unpredictable
concepts.definition: Belief that events are chaotic and uncontrollable, so nothing can be relied on or planned for.
concepts.client_wording: Anything can happen; you can never count on things staying stable.
concepts.example: "You can lose everything overnight, so why plan?"
sources: BeckInstitute-Worksheet-Packet-2020 § Cognitive Conceptualization Diagram Example and Case Write-Up
Beck-2021 § Ch. 3 Cognitive Conceptualization

concepts.label: The world is unfair
concepts.definition: Belief that the world is unjust, that effort goes unrewarded, and that one is treated worse than one deserves.
concepts.client_wording: Life is unfair; whatever I do, I get a raw deal.
concepts.example: "Other people get the breaks. I never do."
sources: Greenberger-Padesky-2016 § Ch. 15 Understanding Your Anger, Guilt, and Shame

concepts.label: The world is too demanding
concepts.definition: Belief that life makes excessive demands and sets obstacles one cannot overcome; the world element of Beck's depressive cognitive triad.
concepts.client_wording: Life is just too hard; everything is an uphill battle.
concepts.example: "Every single thing is a struggle. It's too much."
sources: Beck-etal-2024 § Ch. 1 Overview

concepts.label: The future is hopeless
concepts.definition: Belief that things will never improve and one's problems are permanent; the future element of Beck's cognitive triad. Prompts risk assessment.
concepts.client_wording: Things will never get better for me.
concepts.example: "It's always going to be like this. There's no point."
sources: Beck-etal-2024 § Ch. 1 Overview
Beck-etal-1974 § Hopelessness Scale

concepts.label: The future is threatening
concepts.definition: Belief that the future holds likely danger or catastrophe, so one must anticipate and prepare for the worst.
concepts.client_wording: Something bad is coming, and I need to be ready for it.
concepts.example: "What if I lose my job and we lose the house?"
sources: Young-etal-2003 § Ch. 1 Schema Therapy: Conceptual Model (early maladaptive schemas)
BeckInstitute-Worksheet-Packet-2020 § Cognitive Conceptualization Diagram Example and Case Write-Up

concepts.label: Future ruined or foreshortened
concepts.definition: Belief that one's life has been permanently damaged and a normal future is lost; common after trauma.
concepts.client_wording: My life is ruined; I'll never have a normal future.
concepts.example: "After what happened, I'll never have a normal life again."
sources: Ehlers-Clark-2000 § Excessively negative appraisals and sense of current threat
Foa-etal-1999 § Negative Cognitions About Self factor
